title: [lab · T6] Economics — track thread
body:
> **L.A.B. track thread.** One per track. Ask here rather than opening a new thread — the
> answers accumulate where the next person will look.
>
> **Labs:** L10 · **Lifecycle stage:** Viability · [the method](https://github.com/akash-coded/nanorag/blob/main/docs/80-lab/README.md)

## What this track is about

Generation tokens are about a third of a real monthly bill. The per-query number is the part above the water.

## Where people get stuck

The cache threshold is where people optimise the wrong thing. A false hit is a confidently wrong answer to a *different question*; a missed hit costs a fraction of a cent. Those are not symmetric, so you choose the operating point on precision and **report** the hit rate rather than targeting it.

## How to ask here

Paste **the check that failed and its message**. The messages are written to be actionable — if
one is not, that is a bug in the lab and saying so is a useful contribution.

```bash
python scripts/lab.py run <id>            # public checks
python scripts/lab.py run <id> --hidden   # everything
```

## Submitting

Fork, fill in `starter.py`, open a pull request. The
[Labs workflow](https://github.com/akash-coded/nanorag/blob/main/.github/workflows/labs.yml) posts your results as a comment and
edits it in place on each push. **It will not fail the build on red checks** — the comment says
what failed.

## What this track hands to the next one

Viability produces the artefact the following stage needs. If you finish L10 and cannot say what
that artefact is for your own corpus, the track is not done — that is the point of the lifecycle
running underneath the pathway rather than beside it.
